Summary.description: Counts computed across the whole workspace, not from one page.
Summary.title: Summary

delete.description:
Clear the seeded sample comments from this workspace.

Only the samples are removed: the delete is scoped by the sample Page id,
so comments imported from a connected Facebook Page are never touched.
Emptying a shared workspace affects everyone in it, so it is an owner
action rather than something any member can do.

post.description:
Records a moderation Action. Actions are append-only and reversible,
and never become training labels.

When the comment came from a connected Facebook Page, HIDE, UNHIDE and
DELETE are applied on Facebook as well. The Action row and the Facebook
state are written together: if Facebook refuses, the row is rolled back,
because an Action records what actually happened to the comment.

HIDE is reversible through UNHIDE and is the option to reach for when the
classifier's judgement is uncertain. DELETE cannot be undone on Facebook.
LEAVE changes nothing there and exists so that a decision to allow a
comment is still recorded, which is a different fact from nobody having
looked.

Records what a human asserts the labels should be.

A Correction is not an Action. Submitting one does not hide, unhide or
otherwise change what happens to the comment.

Pull comments from the connected Page into this workspace.

Re-syncing is safe: the provider's comment id is the primary key, so an
already-imported comment keeps its verdict, actions and corrections.

get.description:
This workspace's own keywords. Never another workspace's, and never the
shipped defaults: those are not editable and not listed as if they were.

patch.description:
Anyone may change their own display name. It affects how future actions
are attributed; past actions keep the name used at the time.

get.description:
Public: someone following a link needs to know what they are joining
before signing in. Reveals the workspace name and role, nothing else.

delete.description:
Leave the workspace you are currently in.

Removing a member is an owner action, which left anyone who joined a
workspace unable to get out of it without asking the person who owns it.
That is the wrong shape: a workspace holds another company's real Facebook
comments, and someone who wants no further part in it should not need
permission to stop.

The last owner still cannot leave. A workspace nobody can administer is
unrecoverable through the product, so that guard is the same one that
protects removing a member.
